## Conventions

These are the project's agreed-upon conventions. Follow them in all contributions to maintain consistency.

### commits

- Use conventional commit format (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore)
- Reference task in commit body when applicable
- Keep subject line under 72 characters
- Include Co-Authored-By for AI contributions

**Examples:**
- Good: `feat: add user login flow` — Bad: `Added login`
- Good: `fix(auth): handle expired tokens` — Bad: `fixed bug`

### notes

- Add notes when completing significant work
- Include what was done, approach taken, and why
- Note any deviations from plan or unexpected findings
- Keep notes concise but informative for future context

**Examples:**
- Good: "Implemented retry logic with exponential backoff. Chose 3 retries max based on API rate limits."
- Bad: "Done"

### naming

- Use kebab-case for slugs (task-user-login, not taskUserLogin)
- Prefix task slugs with 'task-' for clarity
- Use descriptive names that indicate purpose
- Keep slugs short but unambiguous

### tags

- Use lowercase tags
- Standard tags include mvp, post-mvp, bug, feature, infra, design
- Add domain tags like cli, schema, parser, tasks
- Limit to 3-5 tags per item for focus

### branching

- Use descriptive branch names that indicate the type and scope of work
- Use prefixes: feat/ for features, fix/ for bug fixes, refactor/ for refactoring, docs/ for documentation
- Keep branch names short but meaningful (e.g., feat/user-auth, fix/login-crash)
- Use kebab-case for branch names
- Before committing, verify current branch with git branch --show-current; never commit directly to main.

### documentation

- Write clear, concise documentation that explains why, not just what
- Include examples for non-trivial concepts
- Keep documentation close to code (inline comments for complex logic, README for overview)
- Update documentation when behavior changes

### testing

- ULIDs use Crockford base32 (excludes I, L, O, U) — invalid ULIDs cause SILENT test failures
- Use testUlid() helper or kspec util ulid for valid test ULIDs
- Never use JSON.stringify() for YAML — use template strings or yaml library stringify()
- Playwright E2E tests excluded from vitest — run separately with npm run test:e2e
- E2E fixtures are SEPARATE from unit test fixtures — never mix them
- Use npm run test:shard1/shard2/shard3 for faster local dev runs (~50s vs ~150s). Full suite still required before PR.
- testUlid(prefix) is deterministic unless you pass a sequence; use testUlids() or explicit sequences when tests need distinct IDs.
- In tests that run git commit in temp repos, set git config user.name and git config user.email after git init.

### development

- Use node scripts/bootstrap.cjs for first-time setup or any session
- Use kspec for all commands; only use npm run dev -- when testing uncommitted code changes
- Daemon default port 3456, health check: GET /api/health
- E2E tests manage their own daemon — do NOT start one manually
- Web UI dev server on port 5173, connects to daemon on 3456
- Regenerate kspec-agents.md (kspec agents generate) after changing conventions, workflows, skills, or agent template files (templates/agents-sections/)
- For shadow branch issues, run kspec shadow status/repair/sync from project root; do not run manual git worktree commands inside .kspec/.
- When command payloads include $, <, >, or multi-line text, use file-based payloads or quoted heredocs to avoid shell interpolation.

### ci

- File watcher tests skip in CI — GitHub Actions does not support recursive fs.watch
- E2E port hardcoded at 3456 — tests cannot run in parallel on same machine
- GitHub Pages needs BASE_PATH=/kynetic-spec for local static builds; CI handles automatically

### cli-lookups

- Use kspec CLI commands (item get, task get, search, trait list) instead of manually searching .kspec/ YAML files
- When item get shows 'Inherited from @trait-slug', run kspec item get @trait-slug to resolve — do NOT grep YAML files
- Use kspec search for keyword lookups instead of piping kspec item list through grep
- Key skills include CLI Lookups tables — check those first for the right command to use

## Workflows

Available workflows:

- **spec-first**: Check spec coverage before implementing changes.
Core principle: If changing behavior and spec doesn't cover it,
update the spec first.

- **session-start**: Get context at the beginning of a work session.

- **task-lifecycle**: Complete a task properly with notes and cleanup.

- **inbox-triage**: Triage inbox items during session context review.

- **codebase-audit**: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Five-phase workflow: parallel exploration (docs, code, config, tests, specs), compilation by severity, interactive triage, execution, and summary.
- **session-reflect**: Structured reflection after work sessions. Surfaces learnings, identifies friction, and captures improvements for system evolution.
- **create-workflow**: Meta-workflow for creating new workflows. Ensures consistent structure and matching skill integration.
- **task-work-session**: Core pattern for working on a task. Full lifecycle from start through PR merge.
- **local-review**: Quality enforcement for pre-PR review. 8-step gate: own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, test quality, test strategy, test isolation, code quality, regression check, and report. Issues flagged as MUST-FIX. The goal is to find problems, not to approve.
- **session-reflect-loop**: Autonomous reflection for loop mode. High-confidence captures only. MUST search existing before capturing. No user interaction.
- **pr-review-loop**: PR review subagent workflow for loop mode. Runs local review (own + trait AC coverage, code quality), verifies spec alignment, reviews code quality, checks for regressions, fixes issues, waits for CI, posts structured GitHub review with inline comments, and merges with quality gates. The goal is to find problems and verify quality — not to rubber-stamp merges. Sequential execution (agent dispatch waits). CRITICAL: After ANY push, must re-verify CI passes before merge.
- **spec-plan-design**: Research and design phase for plan-to-spec translation. Explore codebase, clarify requirements, design approach, review for completeness and spec gaps. Concludes with choosing import or manual execution path.
- **spec-plan-import**: Execute plan via structured document import - write document, choose module, preview, import, review traits, validate, start work. Follows @spec-plan-design. Import auto-creates plan record with status active.
- **spec-plan-manual**: Execute plan via incremental spec creation - create plan record, find parent, create specs with AC, review traits, derive tasks with plan linking, validate, start work. Follows @spec-plan-design.
- **pr-review-merge**: Quality gate for reviewing and merging PRs. Ensures all CI passes, all reviews
addressed, all requests completed, and all threads resolved before merge.

CRITICAL: After ANY push, you MUST re-verify CI from the beginning. Do not trust
prior CI checks - they are invalidated by new commits. Never merge without fresh
CI verification on the current HEAD.

- **task-work-loop**: Loop variant of task-work-session for autonomous agents. Auto-filters to automation-eligible tasks, auto-resolves decisions. Task selection: needs_work > in_progress > unblocking > priority. Includes local-review subagent step and fix cycle handling for needs_work tasks. Verifies work needed including trait AC coverage. Implementation quality: search for existing utilities, match code style, run full test suite. PR review handled by pr-reviewer agent dispatch.

Use `kspec workflow start @workflow-id` to start a workflow.

## Quick Start

```bash
# First time setup
kspec init            # Initialize kspec in the project
kspec setup           # Configure agent environment

# Returning to work
kspec session start   # Get session context
```

Verify shadow branch health with `kspec shadow status` if you encounter issues.

## Essential Rules

1. **Use CLI, not manual YAML edits** — Never manually edit files in `.kspec/`. CLI auto-commits to shadow branch.
2. **Spec before code** — If changing behavior, check spec coverage. Update spec first if needed.
3. **Add notes** — Document what you do in task notes for audit trail.
4. **Check dependencies** — Tasks have `depends_on` relationships; complete prerequisites first.
5. **Always confirm** — Ask before creating or modifying spec items.
6. **Batch mutations** — Use `kspec batch` for 2+ sequential write operations (one atomic commit).
7. **Regenerate agent instructions** — Run `kspec agents generate` after changing conventions, workflows, or skills. These are the inputs to `kspec-agents.md`.
8. **Edit skill sources, not rendered output** — Do not edit `.agents/skills/` directly. Core skills live in `templates/skills/` (+ `templates/skills/manifest.yaml`), while project/local skills live in `.kspec/skills/`. Regenerate rendered files with `kspec skill render`/`kspec setup`.

## Shadow Branch Architecture

`.kspec/` is NOT a regular directory — it's a **git worktree** on an orphan branch (`kspec-meta`).

```
.kspec/.git → file pointing to worktree
  ↓
gitdir: .git/worktrees/-kspec
  ↓
Shadow branch (kspec-meta): orphan branch with spec/task files
```

**Why:** Spec/task changes don't clutter main branch history. Code PRs and spec changes tracked independently.

**How it works:** Every `kspec` command auto-commits to `kspec-meta`. Auto-pushes to remote if tracking configured. Main branch gitignores `.kspec/`.

**CRITICAL: Always run kspec from project root, never from inside `.kspec/`.** If you see "Cannot run kspec from inside .kspec/ directory", check `pwd`.

### Shadow Branch Commands

```bash
kspec shadow status   # Verify health
kspec shadow repair   # Fix broken worktree
kspec shadow sync     # Sync with remote
```

### Troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `.kspec/` doesn't exist | `kspec init` |
| Worktree disconnected | `kspec shadow repair` |
| Sync conflicts | `kspec shadow resolve` |
| Commands seem broken | Check `pwd` — must be project root |

## Task Lifecycle

### Key Concepts

Every item has a ULID (canonical) and slug (human-friendly). References use `@` prefix: `@task-slug` or `@01JHNKAB`.

**Spec items** (`.kspec/modules/*.yaml`): Define WHAT to build
**Tasks** (`.kspec/project.tasks.yaml`): Track the WORK of building

Tasks reference specs via `spec_ref`. They don't duplicate spec content.

### Task States

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked ←──────────┘
              ↓          needs_work
          cancelled     (fix cycle: → in_progress → pending_review)
```

See `kspec help task` for transition commands and options.

### Spec-First Development

**Core principle**: If you're changing behavior and the spec doesn't cover it, update the spec first.

| Situation | Flow |
|-----------|------|
| Clear behavior change | Check spec → Update/create spec → Derive task |
| Vague idea, unclear scope | Capture in inbox → Triage later |
| Infra/internal (no user impact) | Create task directly, no spec needed |
| Bug revealing spec gap | Fix bug → Update spec to match reality |

### Creating Work

- **User asks to create a task** → `kspec task add` — always create a task when explicitly asked
- **Clear scope?** → Create task directly
- **Unclear scope, no specific guidance?** → `kspec inbox add "idea"` → triage later with `/kspec:triage`
- **Learning/friction?** → `kspec meta observe friction "..."` → review during reflection

**Rule:** When the user says "create a task", always create a task. Inbox-first is fine for your own uncertain ideas — but explicit user requests override that default.

### Staying Aligned During Work

**Watch for scope expansion:**
- Modifying files outside your current task
- Adding functionality the spec doesn't mention
- "While I'm here, I should also..." thoughts

**When you notice something outside your task:** Capture it separately (inbox item, new task, or observation). Add a note to your current task documenting what you found. Don't fix it inline — even small detours compound into drift. Stay on your task.

## PR Workflow

Before creating a PR, mark the task: `kspec task submit @ref` (transitions to `pending_review`).

The full PR lifecycle has three steps — **all required, in order:**

1. **Local review** — Quality gates: AC coverage, test quality, test isolation. Run this FIRST.
2. **Create PR** — Push branch and open pull request.
3. **Review and merge** — `kspec workflow start @pr-review-merge`.

**Quality gates (never skip without explicit approval):**
- All CI checks passing
- All review comments addressed
- All review threads resolved
- AC coverage verified

**After merge:** `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary..."`

## Commit Convention

```
feat: Feature description

Task: @task-slug
Spec: @spec-ref
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find commits by task or spec.

## Code Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

Every AC SHOULD have at least one test with this annotation.

### N/A Trait ACs

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

```python
# AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

Group N/A annotations together in a dedicated test or at the top of the test file. The `AC:` annotation marker with language-appropriate comment prefix is required — do not use prose comments or bullet lists. The annotation must be machine-parseable.

## Agent Dispatch Mode

When running as an automated agent via the dispatch engine:

### Dispatch Engine Commands

```bash
# Start background dispatch (daemon must be running)
kspec agent dispatch start

# Inspect active/queued work and loaded agents
kspec agent dispatch status

# Stream live text output from running invocations
kspec agent dispatch watch

# Stop dispatch gracefully
kspec agent dispatch stop
```

### Built-In Agents

`kspec setup` ensures default worker/reviewer agent definitions exist in `kynetic.meta.yaml`:

- `task-worker` — handles automation-eligible `task.ready`, `task.in_progress`, and `task.needs_work`
- `pr-reviewer` — handles `task.pending_review`

Inspect current definitions with:

```bash
kspec agent list
```

### Dispatch Rules and Trigger Events

| Trigger event | Typical handler | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------|-------|
| `task.ready` | `task-worker` | Worker picks up newly ready automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.in_progress` | `task-worker` | Worker can continue existing automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.needs_work` | `task-worker` | Fix-cycle tasks return to worker |
| `task.pending_review` | `pr-reviewer` | Review/merge workflow runs in separate invocation |

### One-Shot Invocation

Run a single agent directly (outside dispatch):

```bash
kspec agent run <agent-id> [prompt]
```

Common flags:

- `--task @task-ref` to target a specific task
- `--dry-run` to preview prompt without spawning
- `--json` for structured output
- `--timeout <minutes>` and `--budget <n>` for execution limits

### Dispatch Loop Behavior

```
for each dispatched invocation:
  1. Agent runtime checks eligible tasks — if none, invocation ends
  2. Agent works on tasks, may create PR(s)
     - Before editing files on a selected task, create/switch to a dedicated task branch
  3. Agent stops responding (turn complete)
  4. pr-reviewer agent handles pending_review tasks via separate dispatch
  5. Continue
```

**When you stop responding, the dispatch engine continues automatically.** Do NOT call `kspec agent end-loop` after creating a PR.

### Task Inheritance

Priority: `needs_work` > `in_progress` > `pending`. Always inherit existing work before starting new tasks. (`pending_review` tasks are handled by the pr-reviewer agent, not the worker.)

### Blocking Rules

**Block only for genuine external blockers:**
- Requires human architectural decision
- Needs spec clarification
- Depends on external API/service not available
- Formally blocked by `depends_on`

**Do NOT block for:**
- Task seems complex (do the work)
- Tests are failing (fix them)
- Service needs running (start it)
- Another task's PR is in CI (not a formal dependency)

**After blocking a task:**
```bash
kspec task block @task --reason "Reason..."
kspec tasks ready --eligible
# If tasks returned: work on next one
# If empty: stop responding — dispatch engine auto-exits
```

**One blocked task is NOT "no more work."** `kspec tasks ready --eligible` output is authoritative.

## Batch Usage

Use `kspec batch` for 2+ sequential write operations — one atomic shadow branch commit instead of N.

### JSON Format

Pipe a JSON array of command objects:

```json
[
  {"command": "task set", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "automation": "eligible"}},
  {"command": "task note", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "message": "Assessed and marked eligible"}},
  {"command": "inbox add", "args": {"text": "New idea to triage", "tag": ["mvp", "cli"]}}
]
```

Each object has:
- `command` — command path without `kspec` (e.g. `"task add"`, `"item ac add"`)
- `args` — object mapping parameter names to values
- `id` — optional correlation label for error messages

### Argument Rules

| Type | Key format | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Positional (`<ref>`) | Parameter name from signature | `"ref": "@task-slug"` |
| Option (`--spec-ref`) | camelCase or kebab, no `--` | `"specRef": "@spec"` or `"spec-ref": "@spec"` |
| Boolean flag (`--force`) | Flag name, no `--` | `"force": true` |
| Repeatable (`--tag`) | Same key with array value | `"tag": ["cli", "bug"]` |

Boolean `true` emits the flag; `false` omits it. Arrays repeat the flag: `--tag cli --tag bug`.

### Invocation

```bash
echo '[...]' | kspec batch              # stdin (default)
kspec batch --file commands.json        # from file
kspec batch --commands '[...]'          # inline JSON
kspec batch --dry-run                   # validate without executing
kspec batch --continue                  # don't stop on first error
```

### Discovering Commands

```bash
kspec batch commands                    # list all allowed commands
kspec batch commands "task set"         # single command schema
kspec batch commands "task set" --json  # structured output for programmatic use
```

Quote multi-word command paths: `"task set"`, `"item ac add"`, `"meta observe"`.

## Shadow Branch Architecture

`.kspec/` is NOT a regular directory — it's a **git worktree** on an orphan branch (`kspec-meta`).

```
.kspec/.git → file pointing to worktree
  ↓

  ↓
Shadow branch (kspec-meta): orphan branch with spec/task files
```

**Why:** Spec/task changes don't clutter main branch history. Code PRs and spec changes tracked independently.

**How it works:** Every `kspec` command auto-commits to `kspec-meta`. Auto-pushes to remote if tracking configured. Main branch gitignores `.kspec/`.

**CRITICAL: Always run kspec from project root, never from inside `.kspec/`.** If you see "Cannot run kspec from inside .kspec/ directory", check `pwd`.

### Shadow Branch Commands

```bash
kspec shadow status   # Verify health
kspec shadow repair   # Fix broken worktree
kspec shadow sync     # Sync with remote
```

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `.kspec/` doesn't exist | `kspec init` |
| Worktree disconnected | `kspec shadow repair` |
| Sync conflicts | `kspec shadow resolve` |
| Commands seem broken | Check `pwd` — must be project root |

## Task Lifecycle

### Key Concepts

Every item has a ULID (canonical) and slug (human-friendly). References use `@` prefix: `@task-slug` or `@01JHNKAB`.

**Spec items** (`.kspec/modules/*.yaml`): Define WHAT to build
**Tasks** (`.kspec/project.tasks.yaml`): Track the WORK of building

Tasks reference specs via `spec_ref`. They don't duplicate spec content.

### Task States

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked ←──────────┘
              ↓          needs_work
          cancelled     (fix cycle: → in_progress → pending_review)
```

See `kspec help task` for transition commands and options.

### Spec-First Development

**Core principle**: If you're changing behavior and the spec doesn't cover it, update the spec first.

| Situation | Flow |
|-----------|------|
| Clear behavior change | Check spec → Update/create spec → Derive task |
| Vague idea, unclear scope | Capture in inbox → Triage later |
| Infra/internal (no user impact) | Create task directly, no spec needed |
| Bug revealing spec gap | Fix bug → Update spec to match reality |

### Creating Work

- **User asks to create a task** → `kspec task add` — always create a task when explicitly asked
- **Clear scope?** → Create task directly
- **Unclear scope, no specific guidance?** → `kspec inbox add "idea"` → triage later with `/kspec:triage`
- **Learning/friction?** → `kspec meta observe friction "..."` → review during reflection

**Rule:** When the user says "create a task", always create a task. Inbox-first is fine for your own uncertain ideas — but explicit user requests override that default.

### Staying Aligned During Work

**Watch for scope expansion:**
- Modifying files outside your current task
- Adding functionality the spec doesn't mention
- "While I'm here, I should also..." thoughts

**When you notice something outside your task:** Capture it separately (inbox item, new task, or observation). Add a note to your current task documenting what you found. Don't fix it inline — even small detours compound into drift. Stay on your task.

## PR Workflow

Before creating a PR, mark the task: `kspec task submit @ref` (transitions to `pending_review`).

The full PR lifecycle has three steps — **all required, in order:**

1. **Local review** — Quality gates: AC coverage, test quality, test isolation. Run this FIRST.
2. **Create PR** — Push branch and open pull request.
3. **Review and merge** — `kspec workflow start @pr-review-merge`.

**Quality gates (never skip without explicit approval):**
- All CI checks passing
- All review comments addressed
- All review threads resolved
- AC coverage verified

**After merge:** `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary..."`

feat: Feature description

Task: @task-slug

```

## Code Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

Every AC SHOULD have at least one test with this annotation.

### N/A Trait ACs

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

```python
# AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

Group N/A annotations together in a dedicated test or at the top of the test file. The `AC:` annotation marker with language-appropriate comment prefix is required — do not use prose comments or bullet lists. The annotation must be machine-parseable.

## Agent Dispatch Mode

When running as an automated agent via the dispatch engine:

### Dispatch Engine Commands

```bash
# Start background dispatch (daemon must be running)
kspec agent dispatch start

# Inspect active/queued work and loaded agents
kspec agent dispatch status

# Stream live text output from running invocations
kspec agent dispatch watch

# Stop dispatch gracefully
kspec agent dispatch stop
```

### Built-In Agents

`kspec setup` ensures default worker/reviewer agent definitions exist in `kynetic.meta.yaml`:

- `task-worker` — handles automation-eligible `task.ready`, `task.in_progress`, and `task.needs_work`
- `pr-reviewer` — handles `task.pending_review`

Inspect current definitions with:

```bash
kspec agent list
```

### Dispatch Rules and Trigger Events

| Trigger event | Typical handler | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------|-------|
| `task.ready` | `task-worker` | Worker picks up newly ready automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.in_progress` | `task-worker` | Worker can continue existing automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.needs_work` | `task-worker` | Fix-cycle tasks return to worker |
| `task.pending_review` | `pr-reviewer` | Review/merge workflow runs in separate invocation |

### One-Shot Invocation

Run a single agent directly (outside dispatch):

```bash
kspec agent run <agent-id> [prompt]
```

Common flags:

- `--task @task-ref` to target a specific task
- `--dry-run` to preview prompt without spawning
- `--json` for structured output
- `--timeout <minutes>` and `--budget <n>` for execution limits

### Dispatch Loop Behavior

```
for each dispatched invocation:
  1. Agent runtime checks eligible tasks — if none, invocation ends
  2. Agent works on tasks, may create PR(s)
     - Before editing files on a selected task, create/switch to a dedicated task branch
  3. Agent stops responding (turn complete)
  4. pr-reviewer agent handles pending_review tasks via separate dispatch
  5. Continue
```

**When you stop responding, the dispatch engine continues automatically.** Do NOT call `kspec agent end-loop` after creating a PR.

### Task Inheritance

Priority: `needs_work` > `in_progress` > `pending`. Always inherit existing work before starting new tasks. (`pending_review` tasks are handled by the pr-reviewer agent, not the worker.)

### Blocking Rules

**Block only for genuine external blockers:**
- Requires human architectural decision
- Needs spec clarification
- Depends on external API/service not available
- Formally blocked by `depends_on`

**Do NOT block for:**
- Task seems complex (do the work)
- Tests are failing (fix them)
- Service needs running (start it)
- Another task's PR is in CI (not a formal dependency)

**After blocking a task:**
```bash
kspec task block @task --reason "Reason..."
kspec tasks ready --eligible
# If tasks returned: work on next one
# If empty: stop responding — dispatch engine auto-exits
```

**One blocked task is NOT "no more work."** `kspec tasks ready --eligible` output is authoritative.

## Batch Usage

Use `kspec batch` for 2+ sequential write operations — one atomic shadow branch commit instead of N.

### JSON Format

Pipe a JSON array of command objects:

```json
[
  {"command": "task set", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "automation": "eligible"}},
  {"command": "task note", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "message": "Assessed and marked eligible"}},
  {"command": "inbox add", "args": {"text": "New idea to triage", "tag": ["mvp", "cli"]}}
]
```

Each object has:
- `command` — command path without `kspec` (e.g. `"task add"`, `"item ac add"`)
- `args` — object mapping parameter names to values
- `id` — optional correlation label for error messages

### Argument Rules

| Type | Key format | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Positional (`<ref>`) | Parameter name from signature | `"ref": "@task-slug"` |
| Option (`--spec-ref`) | camelCase or kebab, no `--` | `"specRef": "@spec"` or `"spec-ref": "@spec"` |
| Boolean flag (`--force`) | Flag name, no `--` | `"force": true` |
| Repeatable (`--tag`) | Same key with array value | `"tag": ["cli", "bug"]` |

Boolean `true` emits the flag; `false` omits it. Arrays repeat the flag: `--tag cli --tag bug`.

### Invocation

```bash
echo '[...]' | kspec batch              # stdin (default)
kspec batch --file commands.json        # from file
kspec batch --commands '[...]'          # inline JSON
kspec batch --dry-run                   # validate without executing
kspec batch --continue                  # don't stop on first error
```

### Discovering Commands

```bash
kspec batch commands                    # list all allowed commands
kspec batch commands "task set"         # single command schema
kspec batch commands "task set" --json  # structured output for programmatic use
```

Quote multi-word command paths: `"task set"`, `"item ac add"`, `"meta observe"`.

### Key Concepts

Every item has a ULID (canonical) and slug (human-friendly). References use `@` prefix: `@task-slug` or `@01JHNKAB`.

**Spec items** (`.kspec/modules/*.yaml`): Define WHAT to build
**Tasks** (`.kspec/project.tasks.yaml`): Track the WORK of building

Tasks reference specs via `spec_ref`. They don't duplicate spec content.

### Task States

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked ←──────────┘
              ↓          needs_work
          cancelled     (fix cycle: → in_progress → pending_review)
```

See `kspec help task` for transition commands and options.

### Spec-First Development

**Core principle**: If you're changing behavior and the spec doesn't cover it, update the spec first.

| Situation | Flow |
|-----------|------|
| Clear behavior change | Check spec → Update/create spec → Derive task |
| Vague idea, unclear scope | Capture in inbox → Triage later |
| Infra/internal (no user impact) | Create task directly, no spec needed |
| Bug revealing spec gap | Fix bug → Update spec to match reality |

### Creating Work

- **User asks to create a task** → `kspec task add` — always create a task when explicitly asked
- **Clear scope?** → Create task directly
- **Unclear scope, no specific guidance?** → `kspec inbox add "idea"` → triage later with `/kspec:triage`
- **Learning/friction?** → `kspec meta observe friction "..."` → review during reflection

**Rule:** When the user says "create a task", always create a task. Inbox-first is fine for your own uncertain ideas — but explicit user requests override that default.

### Staying Aligned During Work

**Watch for scope expansion:**
- Modifying files outside your current task
- Adding functionality the spec doesn't mention
- "While I'm here, I should also..." thoughts

**When you notice something outside your task:** Capture it separately (inbox item, new task, or observation). Add a note to your current task documenting what you found. Don't fix it inline — even small detours compound into drift. Stay on your task.

## PR Workflow

Before creating a PR, mark the task: `kspec task submit @ref` (transitions to `pending_review`).

The full PR lifecycle has three steps — **all required, in order:**

1. **Local review** — Quality gates: AC coverage, test quality, test isolation. Run this FIRST.
2. **Create PR** — Push branch and open pull request.
3. **Review and merge** — `kspec workflow start @pr-review-merge`.

**Quality gates (never skip without explicit approval):**
- All CI checks passing
- All review comments addressed
- All review threads resolved
- AC coverage verified

**After merge:** `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary..."`

## Commit Convention

```
feat: Feature description

Task: @task-slug
Spec: @spec-ref
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find commits by task or spec.

## Code Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

Every AC SHOULD have at least one test with this annotation.

### N/A Trait ACs

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

```python
# AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

Group N/A annotations together in a dedicated test or at the top of the test file. The `AC:` annotation marker with language-appropriate comment prefix is required — do not use prose comments or bullet lists. The annotation must be machine-parseable.

## Agent Dispatch Mode

When running as an automated agent via the dispatch engine:

### Dispatch Engine Commands

```bash
# Start background dispatch (daemon must be running)
kspec agent dispatch start

# Inspect active/queued work and loaded agents
kspec agent dispatch status

# Stream live text output from running invocations
kspec agent dispatch watch

# Stop dispatch gracefully
kspec agent dispatch stop
```

### Built-In Agents

`kspec setup` ensures default worker/reviewer agent definitions exist in `kynetic.meta.yaml`:

- `task-worker` — handles automation-eligible `task.ready`, `task.in_progress`, and `task.needs_work`
- `pr-reviewer` — handles `task.pending_review`

Inspect current definitions with:

```bash
kspec agent list
```

### Dispatch Rules and Trigger Events

| Trigger event | Typical handler | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------|-------|
| `task.ready` | `task-worker` | Worker picks up newly ready automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.in_progress` | `task-worker` | Worker can continue existing automation-eligible tasks |
| `task.needs_work` | `task-worker` | Fix-cycle tasks return to worker |
| `task.pending_review` | `pr-reviewer` | Review/merge workflow runs in separate invocation |

### One-Shot Invocation

Run a single agent directly (outside dispatch):

```bash
kspec agent run <agent-id> [prompt]
```

Common flags:

- `--task @task-ref` to target a specific task
- `--dry-run` to preview prompt without spawning
- `--json` for structured output
- `--timeout <minutes>` and `--budget <n>` for execution limits

### Dispatch Loop Behavior

```
for each dispatched invocation:
  1. Agent runtime checks eligible tasks — if none, invocation ends
  2. Agent works on tasks, may create PR(s)
     - Before editing files on a selected task, create/switch to a dedicated task branch
  3. Agent stops responding (turn complete)
  4. pr-reviewer agent handles pending_review tasks via separate dispatch
  5. Continue
```

**When you stop responding, the dispatch engine continues automatically.** Do NOT call `kspec agent end-loop` after creating a PR.

### Task Inheritance

Priority: `needs_work` > `in_progress` > `pending`. Always inherit existing work before starting new tasks. (`pending_review` tasks are handled by the pr-reviewer agent, not the worker.)

### Blocking Rules

**Block only for genuine external blockers:**
- Requires human architectural decision
- Needs spec clarification
- Depends on external API/service not available
- Formally blocked by `depends_on`

**Do NOT block for:**
- Task seems complex (do the work)
- Tests are failing (fix them)
- Service needs running (start it)
- Another task's PR is in CI (not a formal dependency)

**After blocking a task:**
```bash
kspec task block @task --reason "Reason..."
kspec tasks ready --eligible
# If tasks returned: work on next one
# If empty: stop responding — dispatch engine auto-exits
```

**One blocked task is NOT "no more work."** `kspec tasks ready --eligible` output is authoritative.

## Batch Usage

Use `kspec batch` for 2+ sequential write operations — one atomic shadow branch commit instead of N.

### JSON Format

Pipe a JSON array of command objects:

```json
[
  {"command": "task set", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "automation": "eligible"}},
  {"command": "task note", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "message": "Assessed and marked eligible"}},
  {"command": "inbox add", "args": {"text": "New idea to triage", "tag": ["mvp", "cli"]}}
]
```

Each object has:
- `command` — command path without `kspec` (e.g. `"task add"`, `"item ac add"`)
- `args` — object mapping parameter names to values
- `id` — optional correlation label for error messages

### Argument Rules

| Type | Key format | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Positional (`<ref>`) | Parameter name from signature | `"ref": "@task-slug"` |
| Option (`--spec-ref`) | camelCase or kebab, no `--` | `"specRef": "@spec"` or `"spec-ref": "@spec"` |
| Boolean flag (`--force`) | Flag name, no `--` | `"force": true` |
| Repeatable (`--tag`) | Same key with array value | `"tag": ["cli", "bug"]` |

Boolean `true` emits the flag; `false` omits it. Arrays repeat the flag: `--tag cli --tag bug`.

### Invocation

```bash
echo '[...]' | kspec batch              # stdin (default)
kspec batch --file commands.json        # from file
kspec batch --commands '[...]'          # inline JSON
kspec batch --dry-run                   # validate without executing
kspec batch --continue                  # don't stop on first error
```

### Discovering Commands

```bash
kspec batch commands                    # list all allowed commands
kspec batch commands "task set"         # single command schema
kspec batch commands "task set" --json  # structured output for programmatic use
```

Quote multi-word command paths: `"task set"`, `"item ac add"`, `"meta observe"`.

/*
 * Token Contract Reference
 *
 * This file documents the CSS custom properties that every design theme.css
 * must define for shared design-system components to render correctly.
 *
 * DO NOT import this file — it exists only as documentation.
 * Each design defines its own values in its theme.css scoped under [data-design="N"].
 *
 * Colors (16):
 *   --design-bg
 *   --design-fg
 *   --design-card
 *   --design-card-fg
 *   --design-primary        — Active/committed: buttons, selected chips, CTAs, progress
 *   --design-primary-fg     — Text on primary backgrounds
 *   --design-secondary
 *   --design-secondary-fg
 *   --design-muted
 *   --design-muted-fg
 *   --design-accent         — Decorative + hover: eyebrows, markers, glow, shimmer, hover states
 *   --design-accent-fg      — Text on accent backgrounds
 *
 * Interaction language:
 *   neutral → accent (hover/anticipation) → primary (active/selected/committed)
 *   Buttons, chips, nav links use accent on hover. Primary on active/selected state.
 *   --design-destructive
 *   --design-border
 *   --design-input
 *   --design-ring
 *
 * Radii (4):
 *   --design-radius-sm
 *   --design-radius-md
 *   --design-radius-lg
 *   --design-radius-xl
 *
 * Spacing (7):
 *   --design-spacing-xs     — 0.25rem (4px)
 *   --design-spacing-sm     — 0.5rem (8px)
 *   --design-spacing-md     — 1rem (16px)
 *   --design-spacing-lg     — 1.5rem (24px)
 *   --design-spacing-xl     — 2rem (32px)
 *   --design-spacing-2xl    — 3rem (48px)
 *   --design-spacing-3xl    — 4rem (64px)
 *
 * Z-Index Layers (7):
 *   --design-z-base         — 0 (default layer)
 *   --design-z-dropdown     — 10 (dropdown menus)
 *   --design-z-sticky       — 20 (sticky nav, pinned elements)
 *   --design-z-overlay      — 30 (backdrop overlays)
 *   --design-z-modal        — 40 (dialogs, lightbox)
 *   --design-z-popover      — 50 (tooltips, popovers on top of modals)
 *   --design-z-toast        — 60 (toast notifications, always on top)
 *
 * Fonts (3, injected by next/font in layout):
 *   --font-design-primary
 *   --font-design-secondary
 *   --font-design-mono
 */

─── Content ───
# UI/UX Revamp

## Specs

```yaml
- title: "UI Design System"
  slug: ui-design-system
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Port imgen's design token architecture into kspec's Tailwind-based web UI.
    Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, and animation
    keyframes as Tailwind theme extensions. Establish consistent visual language
    across all views.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI app.css file
      when: |
        imgen token-contract.css values are mapped as Tailwind @theme inline extensions
      then: |
        All 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, and 3 font families
        are available as Tailwind utility classes (e.g. bg-design-surface, border-design-border)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A component using design tokens
      when: |
        The dark theme tokens are applied
      then: |
        oklch colors render correctly and status colors (pending=amber, in_progress=orange,
        pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow, completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray)
        are visually distinct
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A view with loading states
      when: |
        Content is loading
      then: |
        Shimmer animation plays on skeleton elements, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        An active agent task card
      when: |
        The agent is working
      then: |
        Breathing/pulse animation plays on the card border, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion

- title: "App Shell and Navigation"
  slug: ui-app-shell
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Restructure the web UI layout with collapsible sidebar navigation, header bar
    with command palette and connection status, and grouped navigation sections.
    Preserve existing functionality during migration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI loaded in daemon mode
      when: |
        The app shell renders
      then: |
        A collapsible sidebar shows grouped navigation: Work (Dashboard, Tasks, Agents, Sessions),
        Specs (Specs, Plans, Validate), Capture (Inbox, Observations, Triage),
        Config (Workflows, Settings)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        Sidebar navigation items
      when: |
        Items have actionable counts (inbox items, unresolved observations, pending review tasks)
      then: |
        Badge counts display next to the relevant nav items
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The /items route
      when: |
        A user navigates to /items
      then: |
        They are redirected to /specs preserving any query parameters
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The Observations nav item
      when: |
        There are zero unresolved observations
      then: |
        The nav item is still visible (not hidden)

- title: "Task Board (Kanban)"
  slug: ui-task-board
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Kanban-style task board with columns mapping to kspec task states.
    Active Fleet row shows currently running agent work with live output.
    Task cards show key metadata, clicking opens detail modal.
    Not drag-and-drop — tasks transition via agents/CLI.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Tasks in various states
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        Tasks are distributed into columns: Backlog (pending, manual_only/unassessed),
        Ready (pending, eligible), In Progress (in_progress, needs_work),
        Review (pending_review), Done (completed recent), with blocked and cancelled
        handled as sections/indicators
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A task card on the board
      when: |
        The card renders
      then: |
        It shows priority badge, tag chips, title, slug (mono), spec ref link,
        and metadata footer (notes count, dependency count, age)
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A task card
      when: |
        The user clicks it
      then: |
        A detail modal opens showing full task info: title, description, status,
        priority, type, spec ref, tags, dependencies, blocked-by, notes, todos,
        automation status, VCS info (branch, PR link), plan ref, session link
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        Agents actively working on tasks (dispatch running)
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        An Active Fleet row appears at the top showing cards with task title,
        agent name, elapsed time with pulse indicator, and last few lines of output
    - id: ac-5
      given: |
        The task board with WebSocket connected
      when: |
        A task state changes
      then: |
        The board updates in real-time without page refresh
    - id: ac-6
      given: |
        The task detail modal in daemon mode
      when: |
        The user clicks action buttons (Start, Submit, Complete, Block, Add Note)
      then: |
        The corresponding task transition or mutation is executed via API

- title: "Session Stream View"
  slug: ui-session-stream
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View for watching agent work — both historical and live. Renders structured
    session events (messages, tool calls, thinking blocks) from events.jsonl.
    Live sessions show streaming text with periodic structured refresh.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        A completed session with events.jsonl
      when: |
        The user navigates to /sessions/:id
      then: |
        The session events render as structured blocks: agent messages (markdown),
        tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), and thinking blocks
        (collapsed by default, expandable)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        An active session with streaming output
      when: |
        The user views the session
      then: |
        Live text streams in real-time via agent_text_chunk WebSocket events,
        with periodic structured refresh from events.jsonl
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        New content arrives while auto-scrolling
      then: |
        The view auto-scrolls to follow new content, pauses when user scrolls up
        (>100px from bottom), and resumes when scrolled back. A "jump to bottom"
        button appears when paused.
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        A session context panel is shown on the left
      then: |
        It displays session metadata, spec context with AC checklist,
        files changed during session, and budget info

- title: "Agent and Dispatch View"
  slug: ui-agent-dispatch
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
    and active invocations with links to session streams.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The /agents route
      when: |
        Agent definitions exist in meta
      then: |
        Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is running
      when: |
        The agents page renders
      then: |
        Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
        show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is stopped
      when: |

# UI/UX Revamp

## Specs

```yaml
- title: "UI Design System"
  slug: ui-design-system
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Port imgen's design token architecture into kspec's Tailwind-based web UI.
    Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, and animation
    keyframes as Tailwind theme extensions. Establish consistent visual language
    across all views.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI app.css file
      when: |
        imgen token-contract.css values are mapped as Tailwind @theme inline extensions
      then: |
        All 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, and 3 font families
        are available as Tailwind utility classes (e.g. bg-design-surface, border-design-border)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A component using design tokens
      when: |
        The dark theme tokens are applied
      then: |
        oklch colors render correctly and status colors (pending=amber, in_progress=orange,
        pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow, completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray)
        are visually distinct
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A view with loading states
      when: |
        Content is loading
      then: |
        Shimmer animation plays on skeleton elements, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        An active agent task card
      when: |
        The agent is working
      then: |
        Breathing/pulse animation plays on the card border, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion

- title: "App Shell and Navigation"
  slug: ui-app-shell
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Restructure the web UI layout with collapsible sidebar navigation, header bar
    with command palette and connection status, and grouped navigation sections.
    Preserve existing functionality during migration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI loaded in daemon mode
      when: |
        The app shell renders
      then: |
        A collapsible sidebar shows grouped navigation: Work (Dashboard, Tasks, Agents, Sessions),
        Specs (Specs, Plans, Validate), Capture (Inbox, Observations, Triage),
        Config (Workflows, Settings)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        Sidebar navigation items
      when: |
        Items have actionable counts (inbox items, unresolved observations, pending review tasks)
      then: |
        Badge counts display next to the relevant nav items
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The /items route
      when: |
        A user navigates to /items
      then: |
        They are redirected to /specs preserving any query parameters
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The Observations nav item
      when: |
        There are zero unresolved observations
      then: |
        The nav item is still visible (not hidden)

- title: "Task Board (Kanban)"
  slug: ui-task-board
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Kanban-style task board with columns mapping to kspec task states.
    Active Fleet row shows currently running agent work with live output.
    Task cards show key metadata, clicking opens detail modal.
    Not drag-and-drop — tasks transition via agents/CLI.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Tasks in various states
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        Tasks are distributed into columns: Backlog (pending, manual_only/unassessed),
        Ready (pending, eligible), In Progress (in_progress, needs_work),
        Review (pending_review), Done (completed recent), with blocked and cancelled
        handled as sections/indicators
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A task card on the board
      when: |
        The card renders
      then: |
        It shows priority badge, tag chips, title, slug (mono), spec ref link,
        and metadata footer (notes count, dependency count, age)
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A task card
      when: |
        The user clicks it
      then: |
        A detail modal opens showing full task info: title, description, status,
        priority, type, spec ref, tags, dependencies, blocked-by, notes, todos,
        automation status, VCS info (branch, PR link), plan ref, session link
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        Agents actively working on tasks (dispatch running)
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        An Active Fleet row appears at the top showing cards with task title,
        agent name, elapsed time with pulse indicator, and last few lines of output
    - id: ac-5
      given: |
        The task board with WebSocket connected
      when: |
        A task state changes
      then: |
        The board updates in real-time without page refresh
    - id: ac-6
      given: |
        The task detail modal in daemon mode
      when: |
        The user clicks action buttons (Start, Submit, Complete, Block, Add Note)
      then: |
        The corresponding task transition or mutation is executed via API

- title: "Session Stream View"
  slug: ui-session-stream
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View for watching agent work — both historical and live. Renders structured
    session events (messages, tool calls, thinking blocks) from events.jsonl.
    Live sessions show streaming text with periodic structured refresh.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        A completed session with events.jsonl
      when: |
        The user navigates to /sessions/:id
      then: |
        The session events render as structured blocks: agent messages (markdown),
        tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), and thinking blocks
        (collapsed by default, expandable)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        An active session with streaming output
      when: |
        The user views the session
      then: |
        Live text streams in real-time via agent_text_chunk WebSocket events,
        with periodic structured refresh from events.jsonl
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        New content arrives while auto-scrolling
      then: |
        The view auto-scrolls to follow new content, pauses when user scrolls up
        (>100px from bottom), and resumes when scrolled back. A "jump to bottom"
        button appears when paused.
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        A session context panel is shown on the left
      then: |
        It displays session metadata, spec context with AC checklist,
        files changed during session, and budget info

- title: "Agent and Dispatch View"
  slug: ui-agent-dispatch
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
    and active invocations with links to session streams.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The /agents route
      when: |
        Agent definitions exist in meta
      then: |
        Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is running
      when: |
        The agents page renders
      then: |
        Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
        show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is stopped
      when: |
        The agents page renders
      then: |
        Dispatch status shows as stopped with no active invocations

- title: "Session History"
  slug: ui-session-history
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    List view of past agent sessions with filtering and navigation to session detail.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Sessions exist on disk
      when: |
        The user navigates to /sessions
      then: |
        A list of sessions shows ID, agent type, task ref, status,
        duration, and age, sorted by most recent first
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The session list
      when: |
        The user clicks a session
      then: |
        They navigate to /sessions/:id showing the session stream view

- title: "Enhanced Inbox View"
  slug: ui-inbox-enhanced
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Enhanced inbox with triage status inline, quick actions, filtering, and bulk selection.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Inbox items with varying triage states
      when: |
        The inbox view renders
      then: |
        Each item shows triage status inline (untriaged/triaged/acted_on)
        with quick triage action links
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The inbox view
      when: |
        The user applies filters (status, tags, age)
      then: |
        The list filters accordingly

- title: "Plans View"
  slug: ui-plans-view
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View for browsing plan records with progress tracking via linked specs and tasks.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Plan records exist
      when: |
        The user navigates to /plans
      then: |
        Each plan shows title, status, creation date, linked spec/task counts,
        and progress based on task completion status

- title: "Validation and Alignment View"
  slug: ui-validation-view
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View showing validation results, alignment statistics, and issues.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The user navigates to /validate
      when: |
        Validation data loads
      then: |
        Summary shows error count, warning count, valid item count.
        Alignment section shows spec coverage %, AC coverage %,
        orphaned tasks/specs counts. Issues list grouped by severity.

- title: "Dashboard Overview"
  slug: ui-dashboard-overview
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Home view answering "what's happening right now?" with active work,
    status summary, recent activity, and needs-attention aggregation.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The user navigates to /
      when: |
        The dashboard renders
      then: |
        Active work section shows currently running agent tasks (if any),
        status summary shows clickable count cards per status,
        needs-attention section aggregates untriaged inbox, unresolved observations,
        validation warnings, and blocked tasks
```

### Implementation Notes

#### ui-design-system
Set up the isolated clone first. Port imgen's full token-contract.css into
Tailwind @theme inline in app.css. Start with the token bridge pilot on the
dashboard page to validate the approach before touching other views. Create
tokens.css, animations.css, typography.css in lib/ds/. Establish loading
skeleton and error boundary patterns.

#### ui-app-shell
Restructure +layout.svelte with new sidebar component. Migrate existing
Sidebar.svelte to grouped navigation. Add /items -> /specs redirect.
Fix Observations nav visibility bug. Migrate taskDetailStore from Svelte 4
to Svelte 5 runes. Consolidate three existing task detail implementations.
Ensure all existing routes still work.

#### ui-task-board
Prerequisite: daemon must return type and automation in task list API response
(quick fix to packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts). Add needs_work to status
color/label maps. Build KanbanBoard, KanbanColumn, TaskCard, TaskDetailModal,
ActiveFleetRow components. Wire to tasks:updates WebSocket topic. Build task
mutation endpoints in daemon (submit, complete, block) for detail modal actions.

#### ui-session-stream
Prerequisite: build GET /api/sessions and GET /api/sessions/:id/events daemon
endpoints. Two-tier rendering: structured events from events.jsonl for history,
agent_text_chunk WS for live text. Build SessionStream, ChatMessage,
ToolCallView, ThinkingBlock components. Implement auto-scroll with pause/resume.
Port patterns from kynetic-internal's ChatPanel.

#### ui-agent-dispatch
Uses existing GET /api/agent/dispatch/status and GET /api/agent/status endpoints.
Subscribe to agents WS topic for real-time updates. Build AgentList,
DispatchStatus, InvocationCard components.

#### ui-session-history
Depends on GET /api/sessions endpoint from ui-session-stream work.
Build SessionList with filtering. Link to session stream view.

#### ui-inbox-enhanced
Enhance existing inbox view. Add triage status from existing triage API.
Add filter controls. Keep existing add/delete functionality.

#### ui-plans-view
Prerequisite: build GET /api/plans daemon endpoint (wrap existing loadAllPlans).
Build PlanList with progress calculation from linked task statuses.

#### ui-validation-view
Uses existing GET /api/validate and GET /api/alignment endpoints.
Build ValidationSummary, AlignmentStats, IssueList components.

#### ui-dashboard-overview
Build last. Uses data from tasks, inbox, observations, validation APIs.
Active work section reuses ActiveFleetRow from task board.
No aggregated activity API needed — merge recent data client-side.

# UI/UX Revamp

## Specs

```yaml
- title: "UI Design System"
  slug: ui-design-system
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Port imgen's design token architecture into kspec's Tailwind-based web UI.
    Map oklch color tokens, spacing, radii, z-index, typography, and animation
    keyframes as Tailwind theme extensions. Establish consistent visual language
    across all views.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI app.css file
      when: |
        imgen token-contract.css values are mapped as Tailwind @theme inline extensions
      then: |
        All 16 color tokens, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, and 3 font families
        are available as Tailwind utility classes (e.g. bg-design-surface, border-design-border)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A component using design tokens
      when: |
        The dark theme tokens are applied
      then: |
        oklch colors render correctly and status colors (pending=amber, in_progress=orange,
        pending_review=blue, needs_work=yellow, completed=emerald, blocked=red, cancelled=gray)
        are visually distinct
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A view with loading states
      when: |
        Content is loading
      then: |
        Shimmer animation plays on skeleton elements, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        An active agent task card
      when: |
        The agent is working
      then: |
        Breathing/pulse animation plays on the card border, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion

- title: "App Shell and Navigation"
  slug: ui-app-shell
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Restructure the web UI layout with collapsible sidebar navigation, header bar
    with command palette and connection status, and grouped navigation sections.
    Preserve existing functionality during migration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The web UI loaded in daemon mode
      when: |
        The app shell renders
      then: |
        A collapsible sidebar shows grouped navigation: Work (Dashboard, Tasks, Agents, Sessions),
        Specs (Specs, Plans, Validate), Capture (Inbox, Observations, Triage),
        Config (Workflows, Settings)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        Sidebar navigation items
      when: |
        Items have actionable counts (inbox items, unresolved observations, pending review tasks)
      then: |
        Badge counts display next to the relevant nav items
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The /items route
      when: |
        A user navigates to /items
      then: |
        They are redirected to /specs preserving any query parameters
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The Observations nav item
      when: |
        There are zero unresolved observations
      then: |
        The nav item is still visible (not hidden)

- title: "Task Board (Kanban)"
  slug: ui-task-board
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Kanban-style task board with columns mapping to kspec task states.
    Active Fleet row shows currently running agent work with live output.
    Task cards show key metadata, clicking opens detail modal.
    Not drag-and-drop — tasks transition via agents/CLI.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Tasks in various states
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        Tasks are distributed into columns: Backlog (pending, manual_only/unassessed),
        Ready (pending, eligible), In Progress (in_progress, needs_work),
        Review (pending_review), Done (completed recent), with blocked and cancelled
        handled as sections/indicators
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        A task card on the board
      when: |
        The card renders
      then: |
        It shows priority badge, tag chips, title, slug (mono), spec ref link,
        and metadata footer (notes count, dependency count, age)
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        A task card
      when: |
        The user clicks it
      then: |
        A detail modal opens showing full task info: title, description, status,
        priority, type, spec ref, tags, dependencies, blocked-by, notes, todos,
        automation status, VCS info (branch, PR link), plan ref, session link
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        Agents actively working on tasks (dispatch running)
      when: |
        The task board renders
      then: |
        An Active Fleet row appears at the top showing cards with task title,
        agent name, elapsed time with pulse indicator, and last few lines of output
    - id: ac-5
      given: |
        The task board with WebSocket connected
      when: |
        A task state changes
      then: |
        The board updates in real-time without page refresh
    - id: ac-6
      given: |
        The task detail modal in daemon mode
      when: |
        The user clicks action buttons (Start, Submit, Complete, Block, Add Note)
      then: |
        The corresponding task transition or mutation is executed via API

- title: "Session Stream View"
  slug: ui-session-stream
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View for watching agent work — both historical and live. Renders structured
    session events (messages, tool calls, thinking blocks) from events.jsonl.
    Live sessions show streaming text with periodic structured refresh.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        A completed session with events.jsonl
      when: |
        The user navigates to /sessions/:id
      then: |
        The session events render as structured blocks: agent messages (markdown),
        tool calls (collapsible with icon, input/output, timing), and thinking blocks
        (collapsed by default, expandable)
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        An active session with streaming output
      when: |
        The user views the session
      then: |
        Live text streams in real-time via agent_text_chunk WebSocket events,
        with periodic structured refresh from events.jsonl
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        New content arrives while auto-scrolling
      then: |
        The view auto-scrolls to follow new content, pauses when user scrolls up
        (>100px from bottom), and resumes when scrolled back. A "jump to bottom"
        button appears when paused.
    - id: ac-4
      given: |
        The session stream view
      when: |
        A session context panel is shown on the left
      then: |
        It displays session metadata, spec context with AC checklist,
        files changed during session, and budget info

- title: "Agent and Dispatch View"
  slug: ui-agent-dispatch
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View showing agent definitions, dispatch status (running/stopped),
    and active invocations with links to session streams.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The /agents route
      when: |
        Agent definitions exist in meta
      then: |
        Each agent shows name, triggers, active invocation count, and completed count
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is running
      when: |
        The agents page renders
      then: |
        Dispatch status shows as running with a stop button, and active invocations
        show task ref, elapsed time, and link to session stream
    - id: ac-3
      given: |
        The dispatch engine is stopped
      when: |
        The agents page renders
      then: |
        Dispatch status shows as stopped with no active invocations

- title: "Session History"
  slug: ui-session-history
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    List view of past agent sessions with filtering and navigation to session detail.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Sessions exist on disk
      when: |
        The user navigates to /sessions
      then: |
        A list of sessions shows ID, agent type, task ref, status,
        duration, and age, sorted by most recent first
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The session list
      when: |
        The user clicks a session
      then: |
        They navigate to /sessions/:id showing the session stream view

- title: "Enhanced Inbox View"
  slug: ui-inbox-enhanced
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Enhanced inbox with triage status inline, quick actions, filtering, and bulk selection.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Inbox items with varying triage states
      when: |
        The inbox view renders
      then: |
        Each item shows triage status inline (untriaged/triaged/acted_on)
        with quick triage action links
    - id: ac-2
      given: |
        The inbox view
      when: |
        The user applies filters (status, tags, age)
      then: |
        The list filters accordingly

- title: "Plans View"
  slug: ui-plans-view
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View for browsing plan records with progress tracking via linked specs and tasks.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        Plan records exist
      when: |
        The user navigates to /plans
      then: |
        Each plan shows title, status, creation date, linked spec/task counts,
        and progress based on task completion status

- title: "Validation and Alignment View"
  slug: ui-validation-view
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    View showing validation results, alignment statistics, and issues.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The user navigates to /validate
      when: |
        Validation data loads
      then: |
        Summary shows error count, warning count, valid item count.
        Alignment section shows spec coverage %, AC coverage %,
        orphaned tasks/specs counts. Issues list grouped by severity.

- title: "Dashboard Overview"
  slug: ui-dashboard-overview
  type: feature
  parent: "@web-ui"
  description: |
    Home view answering "what's happening right now?" with active work,
    status summary, recent activity, and needs-attention aggregation.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-1
      given: |
        The user navigates to /
      when: |
        The dashboard renders
      then: |
        Active work section shows currently running agent tasks (if any),
        status summary shows clickable count cards per status,
        needs-attention section aggregates untriaged inbox, unresolved observations,
        validation warnings, and blocked tasks
```
